From 101ab946b79ad83b36d5cfd47de587492a80acf0 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Ian Abbott <abbotti@mev.co.uk>
Date: Wed, 28 Jan 2026 15:00:10 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] comedi: ni_atmio16d: Fix invalid clean-up after failed attach

If the driver's COMEDI "attach" handler function (`atmio16d_attach()`)
returns an error, the COMEDI core will call the driver's "detach"
handler function (`atmio16d_detach()`) to clean up.  This calls
`reset_atmio16d()` unconditionally, but depending on where the error
occurred in the attach handler, the device may not have been
sufficiently initialized to call `reset_atmio16d()`.  It uses
`dev->iobase` as the I/O port base address and `dev->private` as the
pointer to the COMEDI device's private data structure.  `dev->iobase`
may still be set to its initial value of 0, which would result in
undesired writes to low I/O port addresses.  `dev->private` may still be
`NULL`, which would result in null pointer dereferences.

Fix `atmio16d_detach()` by checking that `dev->private` is valid
(non-null) before calling `reset_atmio16d()`.  This implies that
`dev->iobase` was set correctly since that is set up before
`dev->private`.

Fixes: 2323b276308a ("Staging: comedi: add ni_at_atmio16d driver")
Cc: stable <stable@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Ian Abbott <abbotti@mev.co.uk>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260128150011.5006-1-abbotti@mev.co.uk
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/comedi/drivers/ni_atmio16d.c b/drivers/comedi/drivers/ni_atmio16d.c
index e5e7cc423c87..b057b3b3582e 100644
--- a/drivers/comedi/drivers/ni_atmio16d.c
+++ b/drivers/comedi/drivers/ni_atmio16d.c
@@ -698,7 +698,8 @@ static int atmio16d_attach(struct comedi_device *dev,
 
 static void atmio16d_detach(struct comedi_device *dev)
 {
-	reset_atmio16d(dev);
+	if (dev->private)
+		reset_atmio16d(dev);
 	comedi_legacy_detach(dev);
 }
 
-- 
2.34.1

### Summary of Modifications

The patch modifies a single file:

**`drivers/comedi/drivers/ni_atmio16d.c`**  
- In the `atmio16d_detach()` function, a guard condition was added:  
  `if (dev->private)` before calling `reset_atmio16d(dev)`.  
  Previously, `reset_atmio16d()` was called unconditionally during detach, even if the driver’s attach handler had failed early and left `dev->iobase` at its initial value of 0 and `dev->private` as `NULL`.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The change ensures that the hardware reset operation (`reset_atmio16d`) is only executed when the device has been sufficiently initialized (i.e., `dev->private` is non‑null, which implies `dev->iobase` has been set correctly).  
- This prevents two potential issues during clean-up after a failed attach:  
  1. Writing to low I/O port addresses (due to `dev->iobase` still being 0).  
  2. Null pointer dereferences (due to `dev->private` being `NULL`).  
- The fix directly addresses the root cause described in the commit message and is minimal, relying on the established initialization order where `dev->iobase` is set before `dev->private`.

Here is the commit message:
comedi: ni_atmio16d: Fix invalid clean-up after failed attach

If the driver's COMEDI "attach" handler function (`atmio16d_attach()`)
returns an error, the COMEDI core will call the driver's "detach"
handler function (`atmio16d_detach()`) to clean up.  This calls
`reset_atmio16d()` unconditionally, but depending on where the error
occurred in the attach handler, the device may not have been
sufficiently initialized to call `reset_atmio16d()`.  It uses
`dev->iobase` as the I/O port base address and `dev->private` as the
pointer to the COMEDI device's private data structure.  `dev->iobase`
may still be set to its initial value of 0, which would result in
undesired writes to low I/O port addresses.  `dev->private` may still be
`NULL`, which would result in null pointer dereferences.

Fix `atmio16d_detach()` by checking that `dev->private` is valid
(non-null) before calling `reset_atmio16d()`.  This implies that
`dev->iobase` was set correctly since that is set up before
`dev->private`.

Fixes: 2323b276308a ("Staging: comedi: add ni_at_atmio16d driver")
Cc: stable <stable@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Ian Abbott <abbotti@mev.co.uk>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260128150011.5006-1-abbotti@mev.co.uk
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

Here is the root cause:
The `atmio16d_detach()` function unconditionally calls `reset_atmio16d(dev)` without verifying that the device was fully initialized during the attach phase. When the attach handler fails partway through, `dev->private` may remain `NULL` and `dev->iobase` may still be its initial value of `0`. Consequently, the detach call attempts to use these uninitialized values, resulting in writes to low I/O ports (via `dev->iobase == 0`) and a null pointer dereference (via `dev->private`).

Here is the patch:
 
 static void atmio16d_detach(struct comedi_device *dev)
 {
-	reset_atmio16d(dev);
+	if (dev->private)
+		reset_atmio16d(dev);
 	comedi_legacy_detach(dev);
 }
